items.finding: The source notes that OH bands in aqueous solution are temperature-sensitive in NIR and MIR, so tempered sample holders are necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an aqueous emulsion, this suggests temperature control or measurement may be needed to reduce spectral drift; test whether in-line temperature stability is sufficient and whether spectra need temperature correction.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns NIR and MIR aqueous solutions, not Raman or emulsion polymerisation, and does not address milky white scattering or residual monomer.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E03 ¶12

items.finding: The source varied temperature together with concentrations and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform calibration and validation for in-line monitoring by including temperature variation and using temperature as an auxiliary variable.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is about reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not emulsion polymerisation, and does not specify an in-line temperature sensor or Raman probe.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E01 ¶19

items.finding: Raman spectroscopy is often used in upstream processing because of high selectivity and low water interference, despite relatively long measurement times.
items.how_it_applies: For a water-based emulsion, this could justify testing Raman for aqueous interference, while checking whether measurement time matches the feed dynamics.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns biopharmaceutical upstream processing, not emulsion polymerisation, and does not address milky white scattering, residual monomer, or detection limits.

citation.quote: Raman spectroscopy is frequently applied in upstream processing in research and industry due to its high selectivity and low water interference [55] despite the relatively long measurement times.
citation.label: E03 ¶20
